text:
Bitcoin broke critical support the afternoon of June 23, plunging 3.9% to $62,340 and triggering $717 million in cascading liquidations. This sharp digital asset contraction is a direct spillover from a violent global equities selloff, highlighted by a brutal tech correction on the Nasdaq and a historic 10% plunge in South Korea's KOSPI index that forced trading halts. Institutional crypto appetite continues to wane amidst this turmoil, logging an $8 billion 30-day net outflow across major funds, punctuated by an additional $134 million drained from spot ETFs in a single session.

In stark contrast to the market carnage, European regulatory infrastructure is solidifying. Legacy firms like Bitcoin Suisse and Ripple are successfully securing MiCAR-compliant Crypto Asset Service Provider licenses ahead of the impending July 1 deadline.

This synchronous breakdown across crypto and equities is fundamentally macro-driven. As Canadian inflation unexpectedly rebounds to 3.2% and U.S. Treasury yields climb on fading rate-cut hopes, the repricing of a "higher for longer" Federal Reserve regime is aggressively draining liquidity from all risk assets.
